title: Gaussian profile and rotation sensitivity
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\varepsilon>0$. For each real $\theta$, define $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$, $\int \overline I(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)\le \varepsilon+C R_A(\theta)$, where $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and is zero otherwise, and $R_A(\theta)$ is the probability that $1_A(X)\ne 1_A(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$.
hypotheses_covered: The bound holds for every real $\theta$
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $u_\theta(x)=\mathbb E_Y1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,Y)$ with $Y\sim\gamma_n$, and put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C>0$ such that $\int\overline I(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)\le\varepsilon+CR_A(\theta)$ for every real $\theta$.
